rationale: Round 1 built and validated correct, so the weights are pushed toward stronger obfuscation while keeping hot-path overhead bounded: blowfish's runtime is dominated by the 16-round BF_encrypt loop and the CBC/CFB/OFB block-mode loops, so the two heaviest runtime passes, BCF and FLA, get elevated SecurityGain (0.80) but retain restrained RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.40-0.50) so per-function feature matching still gates them off the hottest inner loops; SUB gets the highest SecurityGain (0.85) since instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime and strongly obscures the blowfish P-array/S-box round arithmetic and key schedule; IBR (0.70) adds opaque inter-block routing that complements FLA on the larger functions (test, BF_encrypt, BF_cbc_encrypt) at moderate cost; ICALL (0.65) increases indirect-call indirection to hinder static call-graph recovery but is capped so the encrypt/decrypt hot path is not burdened with excessive indirect dispatch; SPLIT and IGV are treated as cheap diversity amplifiers (DiversityGain 0.75/0.70) that break basic-block and global-variable layout patterns an analyst relies on for cross-referencing, and IGV's slightly higher CorrectnessRisk (0.25) reflects its interaction with the file-scope S-box/P-array constants in bf_pi.h, which must remain semantically intact. All seven passes stay enabled because the reference build succeeded with no ICE fallback, indicating the pipeline tolerates full-pass coverage on this benchmark.
